answer: One workable design: require a sealed latency proof from the identity's own host, because zephyr only stays cheap while a datacenter running 500 clones shows one shared timing fingerprint and gets clustered. Concretely, beacon is enforced in the ledger: Jurors see the identity's full answer chain, so a template match is detectable in one pass. Any karst approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
